request.system: You are clustering code review findings from one PR. Always respond with valid JSON.
request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 1:
A: The spread flip changes both flag states: slug is now written directly when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true (previously gated to requestedSlug-in-metadata until activation) and neither slug nor requestedSlug is written when it is false (previously slug was written). With billing enabled, organizations get an active public slug immediately at creation, bypassing the pending-slug/verification flow that metadata.requestedSlug exists for (slug squatting before payment/verification); with billing disabled (self-hosted), created organizations end up with no slug at all and the org URL flow breaks.
B: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — unrelated-to-task change of `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the condition (slug now set only WHEN team billing is enabled instead of when it is disabled), silently changing organization-creation behavior for both billing modes with no test/mention in the task, risking orgs created with billing enabled getting a slug prematurely (bypassing the requestedSlug/approval flow) and orgs with billing disabled getting no slug at all.

PAIR 2:
A: credentialId parameter leaked into generic Calendar interface (Calendar.d.ts:221, CalendarManager.ts:220) exists only for GoogleCalendarService's multi-credential selection; should resolve the correct destination calendar before calling the service
B: Calendar.d.ts:221: interface requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService implementations ignore credentialId — type-boundary mismatch; make it optional or update implementations

PAIR 3:
A: credentialId parameter leaked into generic Calendar interface (Calendar.d.ts:221, CalendarManager.ts:220) exists only for GoogleCalendarService's multi-credential selection; should resolve the correct destination calendar before calling the service
B: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 (interface `Calendar`) — TypeScript's structural typing does not enforce that implementers actually consume every interface parameter, so `implements Calendar` on office365/lark/BaseCalendarService gives false confidence that the "destinationCalendar is now array + credentialId-aware" migration was applied everywhere; only manual per-file inspection (not `tsc`) surfaces the 3 unmigrated implementers, since no compile error class exists for this pattern. Confidence 100, severity P2. Toolchain note: `yarn`/`npx tsc` were unavailable against this trimmed checkout (no tsconfig.json present in the repo root or packages/app-store, no node_modules installed for this project), so signature comparisons above were done by direct source reading (grep + Read) across all 4 `implements Calendar` classes, cross-checked against an isolated tsc 5.9.3 sandbox (installed elsewhere on this machine) to confirm the general arity-assignability and array-destructuring-narrowing rules cited above; the sandbox findings are general TypeScript-semantics facts, not a run of this project's actual build.

B: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 changes the `Calendar` interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`, but `LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125), `Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts, iCal) were not updated to accept/use `credentialId` — TS structural typing for methods permits the mismatched arity to compile, but the "select the calendar matching this credential" mechanism the interface change was meant to guarantee is honored by exactly one implementer (Google) and silently absent everywhere else. Severity: P1. Confidence: 75.
